name: gain of social status
description: The sense that you have risen in the estimation of an important social group.

variations.name: increase in responsibility
variations.description: If the new social status implies additional responsibility, it may come with a sobering recognition of future challenges.

variations.name: increase in influence
variations.description: With higher status, your words may carry more weight with others.

variations.name: regaining status
variations.description: If you'd previously lost some status and you get back to where you were, there may be relief or vindication.

variations.name: unexpected status gain
variations.description: If you didn't see the gain coming, there may be surprise or gratitude.

variations.name: expected status gain
variations.description: If you had hoped for or expected the gain, there may be a sense of relief or justice because in your mind, you may have already had the status.

variations.name: increase in power
variations.description: If the higher status comes with decision-making power over others, it may come with a sense of self-worth. Ideally an increase in power comes with an increase in responsibility.

variations.name: too much status
variations.description: Somone might feel they've been given too much credit and may become anxious that they're likely to lose the unwarranted status soon.

variations.name: possession of a rarity
variations.description: Those that have access to a rare and valued asset may been seen as having higher status. For example, a shiny or powerful object, or having an inherent skill or beauty.

commentaries.quote: The gain of status is a special case of 'gaining' in general. It's highlighted here because for most of us, it's our most important asset. Even money is less important because at least you can couch surf if you have friends.
We are deeply social creatures as reflected in the powerful positive brain chemicals that help align our behavior with our chosen groups.

conditions: The sense that you have risen in the estimation of an important social group.
